title: What Happens If You Get Struck by Lightning?
sources: NWS (NOAA), 'How Hot Is Lightning?' (lightning can heat the air it passes through to 50,000 degrees Fahrenheit, 5 times hotter than the surface of the sun): https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-temperature

NWS (NOAA), 'How Dangerous is Lightning?' (only about 10% of people who are struck by lightning are killed, leaving 90% with various degrees of disability): https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-odds

Tadler M et al., 'Multi-organ injuries due to a lightning strike', Case Reports in Plastic Surgery & Hand Surgery 2017, NIH PMC (flashover: the lightning current does not break the skin resistance and passes over the skin surface into the ground; cardiac arrest and ventricular fibrillation are the most serious cardiac complications, usually fatal unless resuscitation starts immediately; Lichtenberg figures are a transient reddish ferning pattern on the skin): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5253516/

NWS (NOAA), 'Medical Aspects of Lightning' (lightning is primarily an injury to the nervous system; people who do not suffer cardiac arrest at the time may have lesser symptoms; serious burns seldom occur): https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning-medical

Byard RW, 'Lichtenberg figures: morphological findings', Forensic Sci Med Pathol 2023, NIH PMC (transient lines of erythema with a fern-like pattern; appear approximately 1 h after a strike; they are not burns; fade within hours in survivors; seen in only 17-33% of lightning cases): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10329080/

NWS (NOAA), 'Dr. Lightning' victims guide (lightning victims do not carry an electrical charge, are safe to touch and may need urgent medical attention; call 9-1-1, begin CPR and use an AED if available): https://www.weather.gov/media/safety/Dr_Lightning_Guide-Victims.pdf
NWS (NOAA), 'Lightning Safety' ('When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors'; the only completely safe action is to get inside a safe building or vehicle): https://www.weather.gov/safety/lightning

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Hyponatremia' (too much water dilutes blood sodium; severe cases can cause swelling in tissues, including the brain): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/17762-hyponatremia

lines.text: What happens if you get struck by lightning?
Most people actually survive, but some get a weird souvenir.
lines.caps: MOST *PEOPLE | ACTUALLY *SURVIVE | BUT *SOME GET | A WEIRD *SOUVENIR

lines.text: The bolt heats the air around it five times hotter than the sun's surface,
lines.caps: THE *BOLT | HEATS THE *AIR | 5 TIMES *HOTTER | THAN THE *SUN

lines.text: but the current can skim over your skin instead of going through you.
lines.caps: BUT THE *CURRENT | CAN *SKIM | OVER YOUR *SKIN | INSTEAD OF *GOING | *THROUGH YOU

lines.text: In fact, about nine in ten people who get struck survive.
The real danger? Your heart can suddenly stop.
The souvenir? About an hour later, a red fern can spread across your skin.
lines.caps: THE *SOUVENIR? | ABOUT AN *HOUR | A RED *FERN | ACROSS YOUR *SKIN

lines.text: It's called a Lichtenberg figure. Not a burn, and it fades within hours.
If someone gets struck, they're safe to touch, so call nine-one-one and start CPR.
lines.caps: IF *SOMEONE | GETS *STRUCK | THEY'RE *SAFE | TO *TOUCH | CALL *911 | START *CPR

lines.text: So when thunder roars, go indoors.

lines.text: and why it can make your brain swell.
